title: Multi-zone Alpine Glacier Editorial: Light, Distortion, Sky Blending, and Focus with Photoshop

date.basis: Embedded creation_time in metadata; transcript does not provide an explicit production date.

locations.name: Denmark Peak
locations.basis: Explicit mention in transcript as a named peak during the discussion of composition; timestamp 00:45:40–00:46:41.

summary: This tutorial-style video presents a landscape photographer’s Photoshop workflow for a high-alpine glacier scene. The instructor tracks light direction, builds a strong tonal path toward the source of light, and uses exposure/shadows/blacks adjustments to reveal shadow detail and guide the viewer’s eye. The session then demonstrates form-shaping with a simulated wide-angle look (adaptive wide-angle filter at 8mm with fisheye distortion), followed by perspective warp and the rule of trapezoids to exaggerate spatial depth. The workflow proceeds through multi-zone edits—cropping, horizon placement, and zone-specific adjustments for the sky, moraine, glacier, and foreground—before diving into RAW-based color and tone work (whites, color temperature, tint, clarity) and selective painting to craft texture and light. The latter portions cover advanced sky work: blending two skies from different exposures with perspective corrections and cloning, then applying a six-zone framework (mountains, sun, river, foliage, rocks, and sky) for fine-tuning. The video culminates with notes on focal-point emphasis (e.g., Denmark Peak), sunrise styling options, sun glow, flare reduction, and a candid reflection on the labor involved in high-detail multi-shot composites.

sections.title: Initial assessment: light, composition, and planning
sections.description: The speaker identifies a hazy, low-contrast glacier shot with mountains and lenticular clouds. He emphasizes leading the eye toward the light source and notes the need to subdue a dominating highlight while preserving a path of light through the frame.

sections.title: Form-shaping and distortion prep: crop, horizon, and wide-angle effect
sections.description: Discussion moves to establishing a tighter crop, centering the horizon, and applying an adaptive wide-angle filter to simulate a wide-angle look by shrinking the center and expanding the periphery. The technique includes painting distortion into the sky via a history brush and introducing the perspective-warp/perspective-trap-like approach.

sections.title: Local tone shaping: RAW workflow and sky treatment
sections.description: The workflow switches to targeted tone work: recovering shadow detail, leveling highlights, expanding dynamic range, and using Whites to sculpt the sky. The presenter demonstrates color temperature/tint to shift mood and paints a balanced sky primarily on the left, explaining history-based, non-destructive editing.

sections.title: Foreground texture, moraine emphasis, and scene cohesion
sections.description: Attention shifts to the foreground and moraine texture. A second clarity pass and selective painting emphasize the ridge texture and link the foreground to the backlit mountains. The speaker cautions against overly contrasty skies behind mountains and argues for a smooth, diffuse sky.

sections.title: Sky stitching across shots: alignment, perspective, and blending
sections.description: Two separate skies are blended to harmonize exposure and mood. The process includes matching sky areas via perspective corrections, trapezoid-based warping, and cloning to create a seamless composite while preserving sun/star details and cloud structure.

sections.title: Final polish: six-zone workflow, sunrise option, and emphasis on focal points
concepts: six-zone processing (mountains, sun, river, foliage, rocks, sky)
sections.description: The instructor outlines a comprehensive six-zone workflow for final polish, explores potential sunrise styling, and demonstrates selective color and glow around the sun. He also discusses flare control and reinforces focus on a key focal point—Denmark Peak—to guide composition and depth.

featured_techniques.technique: Exposure balancing for directional light and eye guidance (reduce exposure; lift shadows; raise blacks)
Adaptive wide-angle filter to simulate ultra-wide perspective (8mm, fisheye distortion)
Perspective warp and trapezoid-based distortion to emulate wide-angle geometry
History brush used as a non-destructive, state-based tool to apply localized distortion
Dodge/Burn for mid-tone shaping and guiding light path
RAW whites adjustment after dynamic-range expansion; color temperature/tint tuning
Selective sky painting via masking and layered RAW passes
Clarity and local contrast boosts to reveal moraine texture
Sky merging across two shots with perspective corrections and clone-stamp alignment
Focus stacking discussion and manual blending for multi-depth scenes (F4 vs F18)
Sun star preservation and glow diffusion around bright sun areas
Six-zone editing framework for targeted tonal work
Dehaze with selective color adjustments and controlled blue saturation interplay
Sun glow diffusion and color grading around solar highlights
AI-based flare removal as a quick cleanup step
In-scene focal-point emphasis (Denmark Peak) through light bleed and selective clarity
